title: Welcome to Chapter 13: Sharing Our Feelings
text: Today, we are going to learn about how we communicate and care for people around us, especially those who might experience the world differently.

title: Step 1: The Hook - The Mystery of the Dark Room
text: Imagine you are in a completely dark room. There is a book on the table, and you want to read it. But there is no light! How would you know what is written in the book?

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking
text: If your eyes are closed, and you cannot see the words, what other sense could you use to understand what is in front of you? Could your hands help you 'see'?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - Feeling the Bumps
content.description: Just like you can feel the bumps on a rough stone, some books have raised dots that you can feel with your fingers.

title: Step 4: The Reveal - Braille Script
text: People who cannot see use a special way of reading and writing called the Braille script. It is written on thick paper by making a row of raised dots with a pointed tool. You read it by running your fingers over the dots using the sense of Sparsh (Touch)! It was invented by a man named Louis Braille.

content.definition: A special system of raised dots used by visually impaired people to read and write.
People who have partial or complete loss of sight.

content.title: Fun Fact!
content.text: Braille is based on just six dots. By arranging these six dots in different ways, you can write any letter of the alphabet!

content.question: How do you read a Braille book?
options: By running fingers over raised dots

title: Step 6: Reflection
text: Close your eyes and ask a friend to hand you a coin, an eraser, or a pencil. Try to guess what it is just by touching it. You are using the exact same sense that helps people read Braille!

title: Step 7: Connection
text: Our five senses are connected. When one sense (like sight) is weak, our brain makes other senses (like touch or hearing) stronger. This is why people who cannot see often have excellent hearing!

content.title: Step 8: Mastery - Try It Out!
content.text: Find a piece of cardboard and a blunt pencil. Try pressing dots into the cardboard to create the first letter of your name. Close your eyes and feel the dots.

title: Concept 2: Caring for our Elders
text: Let's explore another important part of sharing our feelings—caring for our elderly family members.

title: Step 1: The Hook
text: Have you noticed that your grandfather might ask you to speak a little louder, or your grandmother might walk a little slower than you do?

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking
text: Why do our bodies change as we get older? What happens to our eyes, ears, and muscles when we age?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - The Aging Body
content.description: Just like a toy car might slow down after running for a long time, our bodies also slow down as they age. Senses like hearing and sight can become weaker.

title: Step 4: The Reveal - Empathy and Care
text: As people grow old, our Dada-Dadi (Grandparents) often need our help with reading, walking, or just understanding things. Sharing our feelings with them, talking to them, and being patient is the best way to show our love.

content.title: Be Patient
content.text: Never get angry if an old person asks you to repeat yourself. Their hearing is weak, and they just want to understand you better!

content.question: What happens to many people as they grow old?
options: Their hearing and sight may become weak

title: Step 6: Reflection
text: Think of one thing you do with your grandparents that makes them smile. Is it reading them the newspaper? Or just sitting and talking with them?

title: Step 7: Connection
text: When we care for our elders, we are building a strong, happy family. Sharing our feelings builds trust and love between different generations.

content.title: Step 8: Mastery - The Interview
content.text: Spend 10 minutes talking to an elderly person in your home or neighborhood. Ask them what games they played when they were your age. Listen carefully and share your feelings with them!
